proposals.title: Confidence is the Check button: Sure / Unsure / Guess, with calibration and confident errors fixed first
proposals.what:
Once a choice is selected (or a valid grid-in is typed), the footer's single Check pill becomes a three-part split: `Check · Sure` (the orange pill, Enter), `Unsure` (.btn, Shift+Enter) and `Guess` (.quiet, key I). This replaces the spec's opt-in 'I'm guessing' chip. Each option submits in one tap, so there is no extra step. prefs.confidence = ask (default) | off (a plain Check files as Sure).

How each answer files:
- Guess: counts half (R8), as the guess chip does now.
- Unsure and right: files normally and opens a light 'Unsure' item (R9 kind unsure, owed 1) that closes after one clean Sure answer.
- Sure and wrong (a confident error):
  - the verdict adds 'You were sure. This is the mistake to fix first.';
  - the explanation opens by default;
  - the trap opens with owed 3 instead of 2;
  - coach() and _pick rank confident-error traps above other open traps, and 'Why this one' says 'You were sure of this one and missed it (Sep 22)'.

Summary, new Calibration block:
- Three rows with bars: `Sure 14 · 13 right (93%)`, `Unsure 5 · 3 right (60%)`, `Guess 2 · 0 right`.
- One verdict line, either 'Your Sure is trustworthy: go with your first answer on test day' or 'Sure on 3 wrong answers: used the slope as the intercept, left out the constant term, ...'.
- 'Unsure but right 3: trust yourself more on Circles'.

Elsewhere:
- The navigator gets a Confidence view: an S/U/G corner letter, with confident errors ringed.
- The builder gets a `Sure but wrong · 4` pool chip, and each SkillPanel shows `calibration 91%`.
proposals.beats: None: TopTierPrep has no confidence signal at all. Their 'Mixed' only records a wrong-then-right retry, and their accuracy counts lucky guesses as knowledge. We also beat our own v2 opt-in guess chip, which students forget to press. Here every answer is tagged at zero cost. Confidently held misconceptions are the ones a student never double-checks on test day. Surfacing them, and repairing them with the explanation open (the hypercorrection effect), is the fastest point gain there is. Because every option names its misconception, we can say exactly which misconception the student was sure of, which a bank with unnamed distractors cannot.
proposals.needs: F4: an attempts.conf column ('sure'|'unsure'|'guess'), unified with Tests' qstate.conf and their Sure/Unsure/Guess wording. Traps: owed 3 for sure+wrong, and the R9 'unsure' kind. F3: the UI.workspace footer split and the navigator view. F5: _pick priority and why kind 'confident'. §2.8 keymap: Shift+Enter; I becomes Guess-and-check. S6 and S10 read conf for the report and Review.

proposals.title: Keep-warm slots: spaced retrieval of everything you got right, mixed into every set
proposals.what:
Each (learner, template) gets a Leitner box, computed in progress.record() and cached in boxes(learner, template, box, due):
- A clean first-try right answered at least one interval after the last advance moves the box up. The intervals are 1, 3, 7, 16 and 35 days.
- A miss drops the box to 0, and opens a trap as today.

In every fixed set of 5 or more from pool New, 1 slot in 5 is a keep-warm slot. The builder setting is `Mix in review: Off · 1 in 5 · 1 in 3`, default 1 in 5, pref warm.
- The slots sit at positions 3, 6, 9 and so on.
- They are filled with fresh seeds of due templates from ANY skill, most overdue first, not only the selected skills.
- With nothing due, the slot goes back to the set's own skills.

What the student sees:
- A small return glyph on the rail segment and a `Review` chip in the strip.
- Why this one: 'Due: last right 8 days ago · box 3, goes to 4 if right'.
- Builder header link `Due today · 6 types`, and a SkillRow chip `2 due`.
- The spec's Due pool uses this schedule instead of a flat 10-day rule.
- Summary: `Kept warm 2 of 2 · next due Oct 2`.
- Today and Plan read the due count.
proposals.beats: None for Math: TopTierPrep's spaced review ('Due Today') exists only for vocabulary. In their QBank, a solved item is 'Solved' forever and never comes back. We also beat the v2 spec's opt-in Due pool, which a student has to choose. What changes for the student: without deciding anything, every set revisits old types at expanding gaps and mixes them with new ones. Spaced, interleaved retrieval is the most robust retention effect known, so September's skills are still there on test day. It can only run this way because each template makes a fresh seed, so a review question is never a remembered item.
proposals.needs: F4: a boxes table or a derived query, updated in progress.record. F5: drill._pick slot logic, why kind 'due', and a warm field on the body (§2.6). F4: a prefs key warm (0 | 0.2 | 0.33). Separate from the R9 check-ins on fixed mistakes, but sharing the slot budget. Plan and Today read due counts.

proposals.title: Study one, solve one: worked examples that fade, for new and failing types
proposals.what:
When the next type is new to the learner (0 attempts), or they missed its last first try, the session first serves a Worked example card. This happens when pref examples is on, by default in untimed instant sets.
- It is a fresh seed in UI.workspace's read-only review mode, headed `Worked example · Count solutions`.
- The key is marked.
- The rationale is split into numbered steps: the clause before ', so ' or '; ' is step 1, the rest is the conclusion. 294 of 386 current rationales split this way.
- Every distractor's misconception sits under it.
- One prompt, 'Read it, then solve one like it.', and the button `My turn →` (Enter).

The fade:
- The next question is the same template on a new seed. The strip shows `Watch for: <misconception>`: the one the learner hit before, else the type's crowd top mistake, else the first non-filler reason. It is collapsed once answered.
- The third encounter is plain.

Example cards:
- take a rail slot with an open-book glyph;
- are not attempts, but the seed is db.remember'ed;
- do not count toward the set length.

On demand: a quiet `Show me a worked one` under any unanswered question opens a sheet with another seed of the type fully worked. The current question stays, and its attempt files as helped (counts half, cannot close a trap).

Summary: `3 examples studied · solved 3 of 3 after`.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's Explanation, which appears only after you check and covers only that one item. Their fixed bank cannot hand you a matching second item to try the method on right away. A novice meeting a new type now reads a solved one first and then solves a twin. The worked-example effect is among the strongest findings in math learning. It stops first sightings from being filed as mistakes, and from putting students off.
proposals.needs: F3: UI.workspace example mode, built on the review mode. F5: cfg.examples, and a served kind 'example' left out of counts and filing. F4: an attempts.helped flag, with R8 guess semantics. T-bank later: optional Item.steps to replace the rationale split. A check script prints how many rationales split.

proposals.title: Points map: which skills are costing you test questions, and the points each set banks
proposals.what:
Expected test questions per skill = the domain's count (15/15/7/7 of 44, blueprint.DOMAIN_SPLIT) × the skill's share of College Board's own question bank in that domain. The shares come from the teardown's QB counts, stored as a constant. For example:
- Linear functions: 170/615 → ≈4.1 a test.
- Nonlinear functions: 258/538 → ≈7.2.
- Circles: 67/348 → ≈1.3.
- Evaluating statistical claims: 12/420 → ≈0.2.

Expected misses = that count × (1 − p).
- p is the learner's first-try accuracy in the skill over its last 40 answers.
- It is re-weighted to module 1's 7/8/7 tier mix.
- It is shrunk toward 50% with 5 pseudo-answers, so a barely-tried skill reads neither 0 nor 100.

Where it shows:
- SkillRow: a column `≈1.6 of 4.1 test questions lost`, with a bar.
- DomainCard: the sum.
- Page header: `≈9.4 of 44 lost · biggest: Nonlinear functions 2.3`.
- Sort defaults to `Most points to gain`, and coach() adds expected misses as a scoring term.
- Legend line: 'From the test's domain split and how often College Board writes each skill.'
- Summary: `Points banked: expected misses 9.4 → 9.1`, converted through scoring.py's section scale to '≈ +10 points'. It is labelled 'estimate from practice, not a test score'.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's skill counts, which are inventory: 1,921 questions, 170 in Linear functions. They say what is in stock, not what is worth doing. Their domain copy '20% of test section, 1-5 questions' confuses people. Now a student sees that Nonlinear functions comes up about 35 times more often than Statistical claims, and that their own misses there cost about 2 questions a test. They put time where the points are, and every set shows a measurable gain toward their score, which is motivation tied to outcome rather than to a streak.
proposals.needs: A skill-share constant in blueprint.py. /api/bank adds expected and lost per skill and domain. progress.coach gets the new term. scoring.py maps misses to points. Results and Plan can reuse the same numbers (R5: one source per fact).

proposals.title: Fixed means remembered: three-touch repair (now, end of set, next day)
proposals.what:
A first-try miss schedules three touches of the same template, each on a fresh seed:
1. The repair right after, as today.
2. A `Final round` at the end of the set that re-asks every miss from this set, shown as a grouped rail block with its own header.
3. A keep-warm slot at least 20 h later (proposal 2).

Closing a mistake:
- It now needs its 2 clean answers at least 20 h apart.
- A same-set clean answer shows `1 of 2 · the second counts from tomorrow`.

Builder 'After a miss' becomes a Seg: `Now and at the end` (default) · `Now` · `At the end` · `Off`. prefs.repairs gains 'both'.

Summary: `Final round 2 of 3`. Today shows `3 mistakes waiting for their second answer`.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's unlimited retries on the same item right after a miss, which only test whether you remember the key, with no follow-up ever. We also beat our own v2 rule, where two clean answers two minutes apart close a mistake: that shows working memory, not retention. The student now has to show the fix at the end of the set and again the next day, so 'Fixed' in the Mistakes count means the trap is gone on test day.
proposals.needs: F4 and S10: the progress.record owed rule gets a 20 h gap (R9 and the Review spec have to agree). F5: a cfg.final queue at the frontier. F4: a prefs.repairs value 'both'. Proposal 2 for the next-day slot. The Today card copy.

proposals.title: Type ladder: 386 question types, each New → Learning → Solid → Mastered, with 'Finish this skill'
proposals.what:
Type states come from proposal 2's boxes:
- New: no attempts.
- Learning: box 0-1, or an open trap.
- Solid: box 2-3.
- Mastered: box 4 or more, which means clean first-try rights spread over at least 2 weeks, one of them inside test pace.

Where it shows:
- The SkillRow sub-line becomes a segmented coverage bar: `23 types · 6 mastered · 5 solid · 4 learning · 8 never seen`.
- DomainCard and page header: `142 of 386 types mastered · 61 never seen`.
- The TypeRow shows its state word.

New actions:
- Preset `Close my gaps · 8`: one fresh question per never-seen type in the selection, then Learning ones.
- SkillPanel button `Finish Circles`: the shortest set that moves every non-mastered type up one step (one seed per type, due first), with `14 questions · ≈22 min`.

Summary: `Moved up: Count solutions → Solid, Arc fraction → Learning`. In the last 14 days before the exam date, the builder shows 'The test can ask these 8 types. You have never seen them.' with Start.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's Solved / Unsolved filter and 'Solved 57 Qs'. Those count items in a fixed pool and know nothing about kinds of questions, coverage or retention. Now the student can see which question types they have never met, and fills them before test day, so nothing is a first sighting. Each skill has a concrete finish line, which keeps them coming back (the goal-gradient effect), and Mastered needs spaced proof, not a lucky streak.
proposals.needs: Proposal 2's boxes. /api/bank adds a per-type state and per-skill and domain counts. F5: pool 'gaps' (untried, one each) and 'finish' (templates with each:1, due first). Plan reads the never-seen count for the last-two-weeks warning.

proposals.title: Pacing trainer: tiered time budgets, fluency sprints on right-but-slow types, and a time-sink report
proposals.what:
Test pace becomes tiered: easy 60 s, medium 95 s, hard 130 s. A 7/8/7 module still averages 95 s (R34), so set clocks are unchanged.
- The QStopwatch gains a thin bar filling to the question's budget, with a tick at the learner's median on this type.

New pool `Right but slow · 5 types`:
- It holds types with 3 or more first tries, 80% or more right, and a median right-answer time over the tier budget (or over 1.3× the crowd's median right time once measured).
- The set shows `Beat 1:12 (your median 1:48)` on each question.
- The verdict adds `New best on this type: 0:58` when one is set.

In timed sets, at 2× budget, one non-modal strip line appears: `2:10 on this one. On the test, park it and come back.`, with `Skip for now` (S).

Summary Time section adds 'Time sinks': the questions over 2× budget, their share of the set's time, how many were right, and 'Parking them at budget would have freed 3:40 for your last 4 questions.' SkillPanel stats add `median right 1:12 · budget 1:35`.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's per-question stopwatch, which resets on reload, and their flat 6-minutes-a-question Timed mode. There is no time analysis anywhere in their QBank; time analysis exists only on their contest pages. Students lose SAT points by running out of time on questions they could solve. Here they build fluency on the types they already get right, banking time for Hard ones, and learn to triage, so one question never eats four.
proposals.needs: F5: pool 'slow', tier budgets in cfg, and the time-sink calculation in finish(). F3: the UI.timer and QStopwatch bar. attempts.ms already exists (163 of 283 rows carry it). The /time keepalive endpoint from the spec. Crowd median time from drill.levels().

proposals.title: Hint ladder built from the bank: rule out a trap, then the first step
proposals.what:
A quiet `Hint` button (key J, free in the runner map) sits under the choices before answering. It has three levels, fetched one at a time from POST /api/drill/{id}/hint, which never returns the key:
1. `Rule out a trap`: strikes one distractor, the type's most common non-filler misconception or else the first named one, and shows under it `Struck: C comes from using the slope as the intercept`.
2. `First step`: the rationale's clause before ', so ' or '; '. 294 of 386 types have one. An audit check drops any split whose first part contains the key's text. Types without a split skip to 3.
3. `Show me a worked one`: proposal 3's sheet.

Filing: a hinted answer files helped = the number of levels used. A right answer counts half toward mastery and does not close a mistake (R8 guess semantics). The summary lists `Right with a hint 2`, and the navigator marks those cells.

Hints are hidden in end mode, the challenge, contests and exams. pref hints, on by default.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep has no hints. Their 'AI Explanations' appear only after checking, and their only in-question help is Eliminate, which the student has to work out alone. Now a stuck student keeps solving instead of guessing and reading the answer: scaffolded productive struggle. 'Rule out a trap' also teaches spotting a named misconception on a live question, which only labelled distractors allow.
proposals.needs: F5: a hint endpoint, with the rationale and reasons kept server-side until then. F4: attempts.helped (or the guess column widened to an int). F3: the workspace hint row. An audit script that counts usable first steps.

proposals.title: Skill probe: find your level in a skill in 8 questions
proposals.what:
Two entry points: a SkillPanel button `Check my level · 8 questions · ≈12 min`, and a builder preset `Probe 3 skills I haven't tried`.

How the probe runs:
- It picks one type per skill label, spread over the tiers.
- It is a staircase: start Medium, up a tier (or to a sibling template at the next tier) after a right, down after a miss.
- Fresh seeds, end mode (no feedback until the end), stopwatch on.

Result card, e.g. `Circles: solid on Easy and Medium, breaks on Hard · missed: arc fraction (gave the minor arc), equation from the centre`, with `Fix these 2` and `Practise Circles at Hard`.

What it files:
- Types answered right are seeded to box 2 (Solid), so the coach stops serving them as new.
- Misses open traps as usual.
- The skill shows `probed Sep 23`, and the coach uses the result straight away.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep gives no way to find where a skill breaks. Their diagnostic route is hidden and empty, and their builder only filters by difficulty. A new or returning student skips weeks of easy practice on what they already know, and lands on the right types within minutes. That is diagnostic precision per skill, which the whole-test diagnostic cannot give.
proposals.needs: F5: order 'probe' (a staircase over labels × tiers), a template sibling map for tier steps, and seeding proposal 2's boxes. The Diagnostic section's forms stay for the start score.

proposals.title: Desmos strategy coach: 'Graph it' on types where graphing is fastest
proposals.what:
T-bank: templates whose answer can be read off a graph (systems, intersections, zeros, vertex, number of solutions, inequalities, circle equations) add desmos: list[str], built from params, e.g. ['y=3x+5', 'y=-2x+20'].

In the session:
- Those questions get a `Graph it` ToolButton. It opens the docked calculator with the expressions entered, through Desmos setExpression, and the points of interest labelled.
- In Test pace sets it counts normally, since the calculator is allowed on the test.
- In examples or learn sets it is logged as a tool used, not as help.
- After answering, the verdict adds `Graphing solves this in about 20 s: graph both lines, read the intersection.` with `Show me`, which plays the expressions in.

Data and filters:
- Per question, a calc_used flag (UI.calc knows if it was open while answering).
- Per skill: `with calculator 0:48 · without 1:36`.
- A builder format filter: `Calculator-friendly types`.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's Calculator, which embeds Desmos in a floating panel and stops there. It teaches nothing about when to use it and records nothing about whether it helped. Knowing when to graph is the biggest time saver on the digital SAT. Here students learn it on the exact question types it suits, and see the time it saves them.
proposals.needs: T-bank: Desmos expressions for roughly 80-120 templates, checked by audit (the intersection or zero equals the key). F3: UI.calc.setExpressions. F4: calc_used in the attempts or cfg per question. The production Desmos key (open question 15).

proposals.title: Name the miss: concept, slip, misread or rushed, in one tap, with slip detection
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep marks a miss red and nothing more. There is no record of why, and no mistake list in their QBank. A student whose misses are mostly careless needs a checking habit, not more lessons, and this tells them which case they are in. Students confirming or rejecting the named misconception also cleans the data behind every 'most common mistake' line.
proposals.needs: F4: the R9 slip kind, plus a kind column on attempts. F3: the verdict chip row. S6 and S10 show kinds in the report and in Review. drill.levels() leaves out slips from crowd stats.

proposals.title: Mix-up sets: interleave look-alike types so you learn which method applies
proposals.what:
A TypeRow and SkillPanel action `Mix it up`, and a builder Order option `Mix-up`.

How the set is built:
- The chosen type is paired with 2-3 look-alikes: templates in the same skill with a different skill label (e.g. percent of / percent change / reverse percent; arc length / sector area / arc fraction), plus templates that share a normalised misconception (78 labels recur across templates).
- It serves them shuffled, never two of one type in a row.

Optional `Name the type first` (default on in Mix-up): before the choices unlock, a 3-button picker of the candidate labels asks 'Which kind is this?'.
- A wrong pick shows the right label and unlocks.
- It is filed as a discrimination error and shown in the summary: `Picked the method right 7 of 9 · mixed up percent change with percent of 2×`.

The sibling map is cached with kinds().
proposals.beats: None: TopTierPrep serves whatever the selected skills return, in random order, and offers no order control. Their items differ in structure, so they cannot build controlled look-alike pairs. Interleaving pays off most when problem types are easily confused. What it trains is choosing the right method, which blocked practice never trains and the test always asks for.
proposals.needs: F5: order 'mixup' and a sibling map built from blueprint.kinds() labels and normalised reasons (the Review spec's same-mistake-elsewhere data). F3: the picker step in the workspace. Skill-label wording reviewed so the picker is not jargon.

proposals.title: Rule cards: your own rule for a type, shown on every fresh one
proposals.what:
When it prompts:
- after the first miss on a type;
- when a mistake closes ('You fixed it: write the rule so it sticks');
- never more than twice a set;
- also from Details at any time.

The prompt `Write your rule` opens a field of up to 140 characters, e.g. 'Same slope + same intercept = infinitely many'.

It is stored per (learner, template), with seed NULL in the R6 notes table.

Where it comes back:
- On every later question of that type, fresh seeds included, the strip shows a collapsed `Your rule ▸` chip. Opening it before Check counts as hint level 1 (helped).
- Worked examples (proposal 3) show it under the steps.
- The TypeRow shows a rule glyph.
- Print adds a one-page 'My rules' sheet, grouped by domain, for the week before the test.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's annotations, which are per item and die with the session. We also beat our own v2 notes, keyed by (template, seed), which come back only on an exact replay, while our practice nearly always serves fresh seeds. Writing the rule yourself (the generation effect) makes it stick. The cue then follows the type onto new numbers, and becomes a personal formula sheet for the week before the test.
proposals.needs: R6 change (F4): the notes table allows a NULL seed for type-level notes, and POST /api/notes accepts template-only. F3: a UI.annotate chip. The print view. Review lists rule cards beside saved notes.

proposals.title: Ready sets: start the right practice in one tap
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's builder: every session means ticking domains and skills, three selects, a volume and a mode before Start. Our own v2 presets also need a second tap on Start. A daily habit needs a start with no decisions to make. The student gets the right set in one tap, and the full builder is still one scroll away.
proposals.needs: /api/bank coach and counts (already specified). POST /api/drill with source 'ready'. Proposal 2's due count. The median pace from attempts.

proposals.title: Cover the choices: solve first, then look
proposals.what:
A toggle `Cover choices` (key V, pref cover, off by default; on by default in Mix-up sets) hides the MC options behind a panel: `Solve it first · Show choices (V)`. An optional scratch field, `My answer before looking`, accepts a value.

On Show:
- A value that grid_equal-matches an option preselects it (the student still checks).
- A value that matches none gets `14 isn't one of the choices. Recheck before you pick.`

Summary: `Covered 8 · 88% right · uncovered 72%`, so the student sees whether the habit pays for them.
proposals.beats: None: TopTierPrep's 2x2 cards put all four lures in view at once. SAT distractors, and ours in particular, are built from the exact mistakes students make, so seeing them first invites recognising a lure rather than solving. Covering the choices forces retrieval, is a classic SAT strategy, and the summary shows whether it pays off for this student.
proposals.needs: F3: the workspace cover panel. scoring.grid_equal for matching. F4: a prefs key cover. A per-question flag in cfg for the summary split.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Measured levels 1-7 from 20 or more first tries per (template, tier), with tier toggles always working, 'Include types not measured yet', and 'measured from N' in Details.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: The db holds 283 attempts, and the spec's own helper reads 18 of 386 types measured, so for months the strip is Easy/Medium/Hard. That is what they have, without their working slider.
parity_gaps.upgrade: A personal level: the predicted chance you get this type right, from your skill mastery and the type's tier (and its crowd level once measured). Filter by `Stretch 50–70% · Solid 70–90% · Easy for you 90%+`, with Stretch as the default for learn sets. It works from day one, and it is what desirable difficulty actually needs.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Three tier toggles with type counts; at least one stays on.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: The same three pills they have, with counts.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Add tier-mix presets from blueprint.TIERS: `Like module 1 (7/8/7)` and `Like the upper module 2 (3/8/11)`. A student aiming for 700+ then practises the hard-module mix they will actually meet. Also add the 'For you' zones above.

parity_gaps.spec_says: 5 · 10 · 20 · 30 · 40 · 50 · ∞ plus Other 1-120; ∞ with Custom becomes a sprint.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Still counts questions, as theirs does. The sprint is hidden behind ∞ plus Custom.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Make `By time: 10 · 20 · 35 min` a first-class choice. The count comes from the learner's own median pace, and the set ends when the time is up, never mid-question. Students plan study in minutes, not question counts.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Untimed · Test pace (95 s a question) · Custom, with a pace alert at 1:35.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: A flat per-question clock, like their flat 6 minutes a question, only tighter.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Tiered budgets (easy 60 s, medium 95 s, hard 130 s; still 95 s on average), a budget bar on the stopwatch, and `Tighten` (the budget drops 10% after a set finished under pace at 80% or more). This teaches the real test habit of going fast on easy questions to bank time for hard ones (proposal 7).

parity_gaps.spec_says: Step up a tier after 2 first-try rights in a skill, down after a miss, within the selected tiers.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It works where theirs does not, but only 57 of 386 templates span more than one tier. For most types there is no harder version of the same template to step to, so the step silently does nothing.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Step to a sibling template in the same skill label at the next tier, and show the zone in the strip: `Stepped up to Hard · 2 more rights to stay`.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Easier and harder split buttons when the type spans tiers; otherwise the same tier on a fresh seed.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: With 57 multi-tier templates, most students will almost never see easier or harder. For them it is plain 'more of the same', like re-filtering their bank.
parity_gaps.upgrade: The same sibling-template adjacency as adaptive, so every type offers easier and harder, each with a one-line reason: 'Harder: the same idea with two unknowns'.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Per-sitting flags (R5), a navigator glyph, and a Marked pool in the builder.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: A list you can later filter by, which is exactly their Saved Only filter.
parity_gaps.upgrade: A mark takes an optional reason (Unsure / Slow / Method?), and a fresh question of that type is scheduled into a keep-warm slot 2 days later. A mark then does something even if the student never opens the list.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Strike circles and Shift+A-D, saved on the server and restored on any device.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Theirs is also saved on the server; ours only adds a keyboard shortcut.

parity_gaps.spec_says: A Highlight tool with wash and underline styles, a per-question My note, and storage per (template, seed) that returns on replay, retake and review.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It matches Bluebook's Highlights & Notes, but math stems rarely need highlighting. A (template, seed) note returns only on exact replays, which our fresh-seed practice rarely serves.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Type-level rule cards that show on every fresh seed of the type, plus a printable 'My rules' sheet (proposal 13).

parity_gaps.spec_says: The key after a miss, the rationale, and every option's misconception by default.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: The rationale is one sentence, e.g. 'Substituting x = 4 into (3x + 5)/6 gives 17/6.' Their report explanations are long-form Justification plus Distractor Analysis prose, so on depth we are at parity at best.

proposals.title: Points on the table: every skill and type priced in SAT points for this student
proposals.what:

- q_s: expected questions per 44-question Math section. It is blueprint.DOMAIN_SPLIT (15 / 15 / 7 / 7) split inside each domain by the official per-skill counts in material/keys.
- r_s: the student's first-try rate over their last 30 answers in the skill, shrunk toward 0.5 with a prior of 10 answers.
- p: points per question at the student's level. It is the slope of scoring.ANCHORS at estimate.mean3, or at the level their practice accuracy implies when there is no test; about 13 points mid-scale.

proposals.title: Zero-wait answering: the verdict paints at the tap, the next question is already loaded, and a dropped connection does not stop practice

- 'I still think it is wrong: send it to a person' continues to the normal report, with the check attached.

- (template, seed) is logged at error level and added to server/quarantine.json, which _fresh skips for everyone.
- The set serves a replacement question.

Settings › Your reports lists these as 'Checked automatically · key confirmed' or 'Bug confirmed · removed'.

So tagging is rules plus a reviewed remainder, and a check script prints 'n of 2,550 reasons tagged'. BUILDER: the tree header gets a Seg 'Skills · Types · Habits'. SUMMARY: 'Stopped a step early: dodged 7 of 9 (last week 3 of 8)', with a per-habit trend. DATA: attempts.offered (JSON habit ids of the distractors shown), written by progress.record. Old rows are backfilled by regenerating (template, seed) at 0.3 ms each.

While covered, the MC options sit under a paper panel with a 'Your answer' field that uses the grid-in validation. When all four options are numbers (practice.numeral), Enter compares the typed value with them using scoring.grid_equal: (a) equal to the key: the key is selected and checked, the verdict adds 'Solved without the choices', and mastery weight is ×1.25; (b) equal to a distractor: that is the first try, filed with its named mistake ('Your 14 is choice C: you used the slope as the intercept'); (c) no match: 'No choice is 17. Recheck, then pick.' The choices uncover and the next pick is the first try, tagged cover_miss. For non-numeric options the field is replaced by 'Ready: show choices'. proposals.title: Your odds on every question type, with a difficulty zone that adapts per template
proposals.what: MODEL: each (template, tier) gets an Elo rating in S8's item_ratings (prior easy 850 / medium 1050 / hard 1250). It is updated by every first try from practice, tests and contests, with K = max(8, 40/sqrt(n+1)). Each learner gets a rating per skill, in a new skill_ratings(learner, topic, rating, n), seeded from the diagnostic or estimate. Odds = 1/(1+10^((item-learner)/400)). Levels 1-7 come from rating ranks within each tier (easy 1-2, medium 3-5, hard 6-7), so they exist from the first answer, marked 'provisional (6 answers)' until n≥20. BUILDER: each TypeRow shows 'Your odds ~72%'. A skill panel can sort its types by odds. The Difficulty control gains a Zone Seg: Comfortable 80-95% · Stretch 60-80% (the default when Adaptive is on) · Hard mode 35-60%. The level cells stay enabled on day one. SESSION: a strip chip 'Stretch · 68% for you'. Details: 'Level 4 of 7 · provisional, 6 answers · your odds 68%'. PICKER: after repairs, open traps and least-used (kept first), the picker chooses the (template, tier) whose odds sit nearest the zone centre. drill.levels()' fixed accuracy thresholds stay as a cross-check once n≥20.

proposals.title: Reports that check the key on the spot

It shows the given values from item.params and the explanation, with a quiet 'Still disagree? Send anyway'. If they do not (an audit error, a mismatch, or two options with equal values): 'You found a real problem. This question type is pulled from practice until it is fixed, and this answer does not count against you.' Settings' Your reports shows the check result.

'Answer sheet only' prints a bubble grid. Every page header carries 'Version B' and a QR code (qr.js, already vendored by F2) to /w/?c=CODE; every question carries a 4-character code. Key pages are printed per version. /w/ PAGE: an answer grid that fits a phone. Rows 1..N have A-D pills, or a grid-in field with the rule line; the version comes from the code. Submit files it as an end-mode set (source 'worksheet') and opens the Summary, with named mistakes, grid-in matches and 'Fix my 3 misses' twins. TEACHER/TUTOR: the set's results, from F6 sets, aggregate by slot across versions: 'Slot 4 · Percent change · 14/22 · most common: used the new value as the base (5)'.
proposals.beats: Their 'Share / Export Report' is a dead button, and they have no print at all. Distinct printed versions with per-version keys, feeding back into named-mistake analytics, need a generator.
proposals.needs: F6: sets of kind 'items' with versions[] (R18c). F1: print CSS. F2: qr.js. R19: access for keys. S2: Classes, for assignment.

proposals.title: Solve it in Desmos: the calculator strategy, loaded with this question
proposals.what: After the reveal on eligible questions, the explanation gains a button 'Solve it in Desmos'. It opens UI.calc docked, with this item's expressions already entered (both sides of the equation, the system, the function and its shift) and the key point labelled. Under it is a one-line strategy, e.g. 'Graph both sides; the x of the intersection is the answer: x = 3'. The strip shows a chip 'Desmos-solvable'. The builder gets a Format-row checkbox 'Only Desmos-solvable types', and the summary reads '4 of 10 were Desmos-solvable · you used the calculator on 1'. BANK: Item gains desmos: {exprs:[latex], point?, note}, emitted from item.params. Families to start with: systems, linear functions, linear equations in two variables, nonlinear functions, nonlinear equations and systems, linear inequalities, circle equations. Authoring is per template, and it covers unlimited items.
proposals.beats: Their Desmos panel opens empty. Graphing is the most taught SAT Math shortcut, and we author the setup once per template rather than once per item, as a 3,867-item bank would have to.
proposals.needs: T-bank: Item.desmos for the families above. F3: the UI.calc setExpressions API. Open question 15: a production Desmos key.

proposals.title: Points on the table: a score-gain forecast per skill that drives the builder
proposals.what: Each SkillRow and DomainCard gains 'on the table: ≈12-18 pts'. It is computed as: the skill's expected questions on a 44-question section (blueprint weight / skills in domain; e.g. Circles ≈1.9) × your first-try miss rate on the tier mix you would be routed to (from estimate.py's band) × the scaled-points slope per raw question near your estimate (from the scoring table), shown as a range. A second line reads 'Reach Strong: ≈ +8-12 pts · ~9 clean answers', from the mastery update rule simulated forward. The builder's Sort gains 'Most points on the table'. A preset 'Biggest gains · 3 skills' selects the top 3. The Action bar adds 'This set works on ≈30 pts of ground'. The summary adds 'On the table: Circles 18 → 12'. New students see 'needs 5 answers' instead of a number.
proposals.beats: Their only 'where to spend time' view is the plan's 'Accuracy by domain, weakest first', which ignores how many questions each skill is worth and how many points a question is worth at the student's level. Their builder counts inventory ('170 questions'), not payoff.
proposals.needs: F4: estimate.py (R16) and the raw-to-scaled slope from scoring. /api/bank: by_tier per skill (already specified). progress: a mastery forward-simulation helper.

proposals.title: Scout the type: see its traps before you drill it
proposals.what: TypeRow and Details gain 'See the traps', which opens a sheet. It shows the type's name and its about line. Then a live example, a fresh seed that is never served later, with the key worked (the rationale) and each wrong option labelled with its misconception and habit. Then 'Traps in this type': each normalized reason with your record ('caught 2 · dodged 3') and everyone's share of misses once n≥20. Then your record and best time. The sheet's primary is 'Drill 5 of these', and a quiet 'Another example' draws a new seed. The builder's search results offer the same sheet on each matching type, and Review's trap rows link to it.
proposals.beats: None; they lack it. With a finite bank, previewing a question spends it. Ours can always show a worked example with its traps named and still have unlimited unseen ones left to practise.
proposals.needs: F3: UI.workspace 'inline' read-only mode (R21). /api/bank: norms per type (already computed for crowd). F5: a preview endpoint that generates without db.remember.
